name: Message
summary: Wraps data in a packet the channel can carry, so that what is sent is a thing in its own right rather than a call's arguments.

roles.name: Message
roles.summary: The packet sent over a channel. It exists as a type so that what crosses a boundary is named and versionable, which is what a call's argument list is not.

roles.name: Header
roles.summary: What the messaging system reads to do its work — the identifiers, the return address, the expiry. Held apart from the body because the infrastructure may read it and the application need not.

roles.name: Body
roles.summary: What the application sent. The messaging system carries it without looking at it, which is what lets one channel serve payloads it knows nothing about.
